title: Assistant Canvas — lightweight composition surface (scratchpad)
content:
TL;DR:
A lightweight, ephemeral composition surface embedded in the assistant UI for building and iterating multi-part prompts / small workflows without leaving the chat. Think: an editable canvas where users drag in tools, context snippets, memory pins, and sampling knobs, then run a composed request and iterate.

Goal:
- Reduce friction for creating structured multi-step prompts and small tool-assisted workflows (search -> summarize -> extract)
- Make cost and token impact visible while composing
- Encourage reuse via small templates and micro-collections

Problem / evidence:
- Users bounce between external editors, docs, and chat. Hard to assemble reproducible multi-step prompts.
- Support tickets show: "how to chain search + explain" and users manually copy/paste between messages.
- Early user interviews (5 customers) asked for "one place to try prompt + tool combos".

Target personas:
- Product builder prototyping a helper (PM/PMM)
- Power user in enterprise support creating reproducible troubleshooting recipes
- Solutions engineer building canned walkthroughs for customers

Core hypothesis:
1) A compact canvas reduces time-to-prototype for workflows by 40% compared to chat-only copy/paste flows.
2) Showing estimated token/cost delta per block nudges users toward cheaper variants without reducing success rate.

Key UX elements (sketch in words):
- Canvas header: name, quick-run, save-as-template, cost-estimate (live).
- Blocks: free-form prompt, tool-call (search / SQL / browse), transform (summarize / extract-fields), assertion (validate), stop-condition. Blocks are stacked left-to-right flow.
- Block inputs: small editor with language-mode, sample inputs, and per-block sampling controls (temp, top_p, max_tokens).
- Live-preview: quickly run single-block or whole-flow with streaming results in a side pane.
- Session pinning: snapshot conversation state or memory pins into a block.
- Templates drawer: small library of community + org templates (one-line descriptions, token estimate).
- Token meter: per-block and aggregated token estimate and cost ballpark.
- Export: paste-to-chat or export-as-playbook (JSON or simple markdown steps).

User stories (rough):
- As a product manager, I want to chain a web-search block + summarizer block so I can produce a short brief from recent articles.
- As an SRE, I want to save a runbook template that queries logs, extracts error traces, and formats triage notes.
- As an onboarding engineer, I want to pin the user's org context (company name, product id) into a block that auto-injects when running templates for different customers.

Success metrics (initial):
- time-to-first-successful-run from canvas open (goal: < 3 min for prototypical tasks)
- % of templates saved to org library (engagement)
- reduction in support tickets asking for reproducible prompt examples
- conversion to saved prompts -> calls to hosted API (downstream usage metric)

MVP scope (minimal delight):
- Block types: prompt, search (web), summarize, extract-fields, inline python (restricted), assertion.
- Run-once streaming result pane, run-history (last 5 runs per canvas).
- Save-as-template to personal and org buckets.
- Token/cost estimator (simple multiplication by hosted token price).

Stretch / phase 2 ideas:
- Conditional branches and loops (for batch processing)
- Visual debugging: show KV cache size, estimated latency per block, per-block fallbacks to cheaper model variants
- Inline A/B run: run-block with two sampling configs and diff the outputs
- Embedding-based block (find similar docs from org knowledge base)
- Shareable links with run parameters preserved (for onboarding/playbooks)

Security / compliance notes:
- Org templates may contain PII — need redaction and retention policy.
- Private deployment: ensure canvas saved templates are stored in the customer's VPC if Private mode.
- KMS/HSM integration required for export of templates containing secrets.

Open questions (parking lot):
- Block model selection: allow per-block model override? default to routing policy similar to runtime (latency/cost).
- Authorization model for org templates: who can publish? review workflow?
- Offline / local runner for on-prem customers — mimic hosted flows but with different model availability UX.
- How to represent multi-turn conversational context when exporting to chat (stitching).

Implementation notes (tech):
- Canvas as lightweight front-end micro-app that composes requests to existing Redwood endpoints (tooling via function calls / tool calling surface).
- Use existing batching/caching primitives for run execution; stream results using established streaming hooks.
- Leverage Optimize recommendations to suggest quantized cheaper models where acceptable.

Prototype plan (2-week spike):
Week 1:
- Basic front-end with block drag/drop and prompt block editor
- Hook up prompt block -> Redwood hosted generate endpoint, stream results to pane
Week 2:
- Add search tool block (uses internal search lambda + function-calling pattern)
- Live token estimator + save-as-template feature (personal only)
- Internal demo + collect time-to-first-run metrics from 5 internal users

Risks / mitigations:
- Complexity creep: limit block types for MVP, keep UI intentionally minimal.
- Cost blowups: require per-run confirmation for > X token threshold and show cost estimate prominently.
- Template quality variance: add template ratings / trust labels before publishing org-wide.

Next steps (short list):
- Sync with UX (Lena) for one-page wireframes (due EOD Fri)
- Book 30m with Infra (Miles) to confirm routing & per-block model override feasibility
- Draft a short experiment setup for internal pilot (5 users, 2 templates each)
- Add to product roadmap backlog: PROD-789 (Assistant Canvas MVP)

Notes to self:
- Keep the naming small: "Canvas" rather than "Workflow Studio" for lower commitment.
- Focus on conversion path: save -> template -> share -> run in production.
- Avoid building a full orchestration engine initially; rely on simple sequential execution and explicit user steps.
